name: Culture and identify organisms in community microbiology
summary: Urine, swab and stool specimens from community patients are plated for culture, incubated overnight and read by medical laboratory technologists, who decide which growth is significant, identify pathogens by MALDI-TOF and run susceptibility tests before releasing preliminary and final reports. Stools increasingly go to a molecular enteric panel instead of culture. Most specimens are negative or contaminated and finish after one overnight incubation, but positive cultures need a second day for susceptibility, and unusual resistance, critical results and diseases of public health significance add reviews, phone calls and notifications. Elapsed time is set by incubation and batch runs, and hands-on time is spread over plating, plate reading and result review.

baseline.org_archetype: A large Canadian community laboratory company whose regional laboratories run microbiology with automated plating, MALDI-TOF identification, automated susceptibility testing and molecular panels.
baseline.notes: About 110,000 microbiology specimens a month, mostly urine cultures, from collection centres, physician offices and long-term care homes.

trigger: An accessioned microbiology specimen arrives at the microbiology bench from specimen processing.
end_state: A final result (negative, contaminated, identified pathogen with susceptibilities, or rejection notice) is released to the LIS, with critical and reportable findings handed to the call desk and public health.

volume.seasonality: Higher in winter for throat swabs and in late summer for enteric infections; weekday peaks.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate of about 16% of community requisitions.
Plating and set-up role from the organisation file; FTE derived from minutes times volume. Loaded cost is hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.

steps.name: Receive and sort microbiology specimens
steps.description: The microbiology laboratory assistant takes the accessioned specimens from processing, scans each one to receive it on the bench, checks container type, label and transport time or preservative against the accepted criteria, and sorts urines, swabs and stools into plating batches.

error.defect_description: Specimen sorted to the wrong protocol or an expired transport time missed.

control.basis: ISO 15189 accredited microbiology procedures (Accreditation Canada Diagnostics, IQMH, MANQAP): specimen acceptance and rejection criteria

next.condition: stool for the molecular enteric panel
leaking, unlabelled, wrong container or transport time exceeded

evidence.note: Microbiology is accredited or licensed at the Winnipeg and Quebec laboratories. Transport limits (urine at room temperature no more than 30 minutes unless refrigerated or preserved) and identification checks are described; specimen mix and the 2.5% problem share are estimates.

steps.name: Reject or query an unacceptable specimen
steps.description: The laboratory assistant records the problem in the LIS with a rejection code, either cancels the culture with a comment asking for a new specimen or, after a call with the clinic, accepts it with a qualifying comment, and logs the rejection for quality monitoring.

control.basis: ISO 15189 accredited microbiology procedures (Accreditation Canada Diagnostics, IQMH, MANQAP): rejection criteria and documentation of nonconforming specimens

next.condition: specimen rejected and a recollection requested

evidence.note: Common practice; branch shares and minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Plate specimens for culture
steps.description: The laboratory assistant loads urine and liquid swab specimens onto the automated plating instrument, which inoculates, streaks and labels the agar plates; other specimens are plated by hand with the media set in the bench protocol.

error.defect_description: Wrong media set or plate labelled for another specimen.

next.condition: genital, wound or other swab that needs a Gram stain

evidence.note: Automated plating is listed among the microbiology instruments in the organisation file; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Prepare and read a Gram stain
steps.description: The technologist makes and stains a smear from the swab, reads it under the microscope for cells and organisms (for example a Nugent score for bacterial vaginosis), and records the result for the final report.

error.defect_description: Gram stain misread or stain quality not checked.

evidence.note: Common practice for genital and wound swabs; share and minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Incubate plates overnight
steps.description: The inoculated plates sit in the incubator at the required temperature and atmosphere until the morning read; nobody works on the specimen during this time.

evidence.note: Culture requires 24 to 96 hours; 16 to 24 hours of first incubation is the common minimum.

steps.name: Run a stool molecular enteric panel
steps.description: The technologist loads stool in transport medium into the molecular panel instrument in batches, runs it for about three hours, reviews the target results and controls, and records positive and negative results.

error.defect_description: Run accepted with an invalid internal control.

evidence.note: Molecular stool panels give results in 1 to 5 hours against 24 to 96 hours for culture; the 9% share of specimens and minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Read culture plates
steps.description: The technologist examines each plate, estimates colony counts, recognises normal flora, and decides whether the culture is negative, mixed and probably contaminated, needs more incubation, or grows a potential pathogen that must be identified.

error.defect_description: Significant growth called negative or a contaminant worked up.

next.condition: no growth, normal flora or no significant growth
three or more organisms, probable contamination

evidence.note: Three or more species usually means contamination and clean-catch urines often contain mixed flora; the 60/12/24/4 split is the author's estimate for community specimens dominated by urine cultures.

steps.name: Reincubate and reread a slow-growing culture
steps.description: Plates with scant or slow growth, throat cultures held for a second day and fungal cultures go back into the incubator and the technologist reads them again the next day.

evidence.note: Common practice; shares are estimates.

steps.name: Report mixed growth as probable contamination
steps.description: The technologist enters the mixed growth result with a standard comment that the specimen is probably contaminated and should be repeated if clinically indicated, without identifying each organism.

evidence.note: Reporting practice for mixed flora; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Spot colonies for MALDI-TOF identification
steps.description: The technologist picks a colony of each potential pathogen, spots it onto the MALDI-TOF target plate with matrix, and records the target positions against the specimen numbers.

error.defect_description: Colony spotted in the wrong target position.

evidence.note: MALDI-TOF identification is listed among the microbiology instruments in the organisation file; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: MALDI-TOF identifies the organism
steps.description: The mass spectrometer reads each spot and matches the spectrum to its library, returning an organism name and a confidence score; the target plate runs in batches.

evidence.note: Batch run times are estimates.

steps.name: Review the identification and decide on susceptibility testing
steps.description: The technologist checks the identification score against the colony appearance and specimen type, applies the bench rules on colony count and organism to decide whether susceptibility testing is needed, and sends low-score or unusual results for repeat identification.

error.defect_description: Susceptibility not set up for a significant isolate.

next.condition: identification only (for example group A streptococcus or yeast)

evidence.note: Common practice; shares are estimates.

steps.name: Repeat or extend the identification
steps.description: For a low-score or unusual result the technologist subcultures for a pure growth, repeats the MALDI-TOF the next day or uses biochemical tests, and refers organisms the laboratory cannot identify.

next.condition: refer to the public health laboratory

evidence.note: Common practice; shares are estimates.

steps.name: Release a preliminary report with the identification
steps.description: The technologist releases a preliminary result such as the organism and colony count with susceptibility to follow, so the clinician sees it in the EMR before the final report.

evidence.note: Preliminary and final reports are named in the organisation file process map description; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Set up susceptibility testing
steps.description: The technologist makes a standardised suspension of the isolate, inoculates the susceptibility card or disk diffusion plate, and loads it into the instrument or incubator.

error.defect_description: Inoculum density wrong or isolate mixed.

evidence.note: Common practice; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Susceptibility instrument incubates and reads
steps.description: The automated susceptibility system incubates the card and reads growth in each antibiotic well, or the disk plate incubates overnight; nobody works on the specimen meanwhile.

evidence.note: Automated systems typically read in 6 to 18 hours and disk tests overnight; estimate.

steps.name: Review susceptibility results and apply expert rules
steps.description: The technologist reviews the MIC or zone results with the interpretive breakpoints and expert rules, checks for impossible or unusual patterns, and selects which antibiotics to report under the cascade rules.

next.condition: unusual or alert resistance such as ESBL, CPE, MRSA or VRE

evidence.note: Common practice; shares are estimates.

steps.name: Confirm unusual resistance with the charge technologist
steps.description: The charge technologist reviews the unusual result, orders confirmatory testing or a repeat, decides on infection control comments and whether the medical microbiologist must review before release.

evidence.note: Common practice; shares are estimates.

steps.name: Medical microbiologist reviews an unusual result
steps.description: The medical microbiologist reviews the isolate, the confirmatory results and the clinical context, approves the interpretive comment and treatment advice, and may phone the clinician.

evidence.note: Medical microbiologists are part of the medical director group in the organisation file; minutes and share are estimates.

steps.name: Verify and release the final report
steps.description: The technologist checks the culture reading, identification, susceptibility and comments against the specimen and requisition, and releases the final result to the LIS for reporting.

control.basis: Medical Laboratory Technology Act, 1991: evaluation of the technical sufficiency of investigations and their results is within the registered MLT scope; ISO 15189 review of results before release

next.condition: verification finds an inconsistency; plates re-read

evidence.note: Microbiology is a listed company service. Interpreting and approving results is an MLT duty; the critical share matches the critical result workflow's microbiology volume and the reportable share is an estimate.

steps.name: Confirm a critical result and hand it to the call desk
steps.description: The technologist confirms the critical microbiology finding, flags it in the LIS so the results call desk phones the ordering clinician, and notes any technical details the caller needs.

control.basis: OAML guideline for reporting laboratory results: critical values phoned 24 hours a day

evidence.note: Handoff to the critical result process; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Report a disease of public health significance
steps.description: The technologist completes the public health notification for a reportable organism such as Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter or gonorrhoea, sends it to the local medical officer of health by fax or phone, and records the notification in the LIS.

error.defect_description: Report sent late or to the wrong health unit.

control.basis: Ontario Health Protection and Promotion Act: laboratory operators report designated diseases to the medical officer of health (Manitoba and Quebec public health laws are similar)

next.condition: isolate must go to the public health laboratory

evidence.note: The duty to report is named in the process map; the 1.5% reportable share and minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Ship an isolate to the public health laboratory
steps.description: The laboratory assistant subcultures or packages the isolate, completes the public health laboratory requisition, packs it as infectious substance under transport of dangerous goods rules, and books the courier.

control.basis: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations: packaging and documentation of infectious substances

evidence.note: Common practice; minutes are estimates.

exceptions.name: Specimen rejected
exceptions.description: Leaking, unlabelled or over-age specimens are cancelled with a recollection comment.

exceptions.name: Mixed growth reported as contamination
exceptions.description: Three or more organisms; reported with a repeat-if-indicated comment.

exceptions.name: Unusual resistance
exceptions.description: ESBL, CPE, MRSA or VRE patterns confirmed by the charge technologist and sometimes the medical microbiologist.

exceptions.name: Reportable disease
exceptions.description: Notification to the medical officer of health and, for enteric pathogens, isolate referral.

exceptions.name: Critical microbiology result
exceptions.description: Handed to the results call desk for phone notification.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from bench receipt to final result
benchmarks.population: Author's estimate for community microbiology dominated by urine cultures

evidence.note: Based on idsa2018 (24 to 96 hours for culture, 1 to 5 hours for molecular panels) and the usual negative-at-one-day and positive-at-two-days pattern for urine cultures.

benchmarks.unit: minutes before refrigeration or preservative is needed
hours to result against 24 to 96 hours for culture

pain_points.description: Overnight incubation and batch runs set a one-day minimum for every culture and two days for positives needing susceptibility.
About one urine culture in eight is mixed growth from poor collection, which uses reading time and leads to repeat collections.

evidence.note: Clean-catch urines routinely contain mixed flora; the share is an estimate.

pain_points.description: Plate reading depends on experienced technologists who judge significance and contamination by eye.

evidence.note: Common practice.

pain_points.description: Public health notification is a manual fax or phone step that can be delayed or misdirected.

evidence.note: Common practice in the period.

sources.title: A guide to utilization of the microbiology laboratory for diagnosis of infectious diseases: 2018 update by IDSA and ASM
sources.publisher: Clinical Infectious Diseases (Infectious Diseases Society of America and American Society for Microbiology)
sources.supports: Urine should not sit at room temperature more than 30 minutes, otherwise refrigerate or use preservative tubes; three or more species usually means contamination; clean-catch urines routinely contain mixed flora; stool culture takes 24 to 72 hours to recover Salmonella and 24 to 96 hours is often required for culture, whereas multiplex molecular panels give results in 1 to 5 hours; C. difficile NAAT sensitivity 93% to 100%; stool not transported within 2 hours goes into Cary-Blair medium.

sources.title: Medical Laboratory Technologist - Microbiology
sources.supports: Rotational shifts seven days a week 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; $36.00 to $43.50 an hour; sample identification and specimen requirements, QC and equipment maintenance, recording, interpreting and approving results, troubleshooting assays and equipment, reporting incidents and nonconformities.

sources.title: Laws and legislation governing MLT practice
sources.publisher: College of Medical Laboratory Technologists of Ontario
sources.supports: Medical Laboratory Technology Act, 1991: the scope of practice is the performance of laboratory investigations and the evaluation of the technical sufficiency of the investigations and their results; communicating a diagnosis is not an MLT authorised act; protected title.

sources.title: Standards of practice
sources.publisher: Canadian Society for Medical Laboratory Science
sources.supports: MLTs adhere to quality control protocols, review abnormal QC results, troubleshoot equipment malfunctions and validate test results; laboratory assistants work on pre- and post-analytical specimen handling and prepare reagents.

sources.title: Licences and quality commitment
sources.supports: The quality management system uses software to monitor quality control of analytical processes, external quality assessment (CAP, QMP-LS, Healthmetrix) for all assays, internal audits and document control; Brampton, London, Ottawa and Peterborough hold ISO 15189 accreditation and Ontario licences; Winnipeg holds CAP and MANQAP accreditation for chemistry, cytology, histology, haematology and microbiology; pathology subspecialties include dermatopathology, gastrointestinal, uropathology, breast and gynaecologic pathology.

sources.title: Wages: Medical Technologist - Medical Laboratory in Ontario (NOC 32120)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low $23.00, median $42.00, high $50.00 (2023-2024).

sources.title: The model laboratory careers (open positions)
sources.supports: Open roles include Laboratory Assistant-Histology, Manager Histology and Pathology Assistant (Brampton), Clinical Laboratory Assistant in cytology (Brampton), Cytotechnologists (Winnipeg), Medical Laboratory Technologist - Microbiology, Medical Transcriptionist (Winnipeg histology) and Charge Technologist (Winnipeg).

sources.title: Hospital solutions
sources.supports: Nine Canadian laboratories, more than 60 pathologists, more than 500 hospitals served; services include pathology and histology, cytology, immunohistochemistry and microbiology; subspecialties include dermatology, gastrointestinal, breast, prostate and gynaecology.

assumptions: Specimen mix (about 55% urine, 15% genital swabs, 8% throat swabs, 10% stool, 12% other swabs and fungal specimens) is the author's estimate for a Canadian community laboratory; branch shares follow from it.
The process map lists the QC record from cl-daily-qc as a trigger; it does not start a case, so it is declared under interfaces.inputs.
Instrument run times (incubation, MALDI-TOF batches, susceptibility incubation, molecular panels) are waiting with no hands-on time.
Chlamydia and gonorrhoea NAAT, C. difficile and ova and parasite testing are folded into the molecular and culture paths and not modelled separately.

Critical results are about 0.35% of specimens so that microbiology supplies about 15% of the 2,500 critical calls a month assumed by the critical result workflow. Cases that are both critical and reportable end with the public health outcomes, so a small share of critical handoffs is not counted under the critical_result_referred outcome.
Medical microbiologists are counted in the organisation file's medical director role.
The charge technologist's stated FTE is above the per-case minutes because bench supervision and staffing are not modelled per specimen.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (hourly wage times 1.35).
